### Observed differences

- In the before window, each of the five closely connected activities A35, A36, A41, A42 and A43 ran before A26 and before A27 in about 98–100 of 100 traces; in the later window the order is reversed, with A26 and A27 running before each of them in about 97–99 of 100 traces. All these activities still co-occur in every trace in both windows, so presence did not change — only order did. [REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020]
- The hand-offs around these segments changed accordingly. In the before window, A25 spread its outgoing transitions almost evenly over the group (about 18–22% each) and A26 led to A30 in about 98% of its outgoing transitions; in the later window, A25 leads to A27 in about 99 of 100 transitions, A26 feeds the group (about 16–21% to each member), and each group member sends about 18–21% of its outgoing transitions to A30 instead of the about 17–22% that previously went to A27. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009]
- Event positions moved consistently with this reversal: A27's mean position moved from about 0.52 to about 0.39 of the trace and A26's from about 0.65 to about 0.52, while A35, A36, A41, A42 and A43 moved from about 0.44 to about 0.60; each of these activities still appears in all 200 traces per window. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008]
- Former close adjacencies largely disappeared: A25 was within five steps of each group member in about 194–199 of 200 before-traces but in only 1–2 of 200 after-traces, and the group members' five-step relation to A27 fell from about 195–199 to 2–3 of 200 traces. [LAG010, LAG011, LAG012, LAG013, LAG014, LAG015, LAG016, LAG017, LAG018, LAG019]
- A02 became much rarer: it appeared in about 32% of before-traces (63 of 200) versus about 10% of after-traces (20 of 200), and where it occurs it now sits later in the trace (median relative position about 0.32 before versus 0.75 after, the latter from 20 occurrences). Its outgoing transitions, previously dominated by A20 (about 46%) and A19 (about 38%), are now spread over many activities (largest shares A52 about 23% and A38 about 14%), though the later profile rests on only 22 transitions; A46's transitions into A02 fell from about 28% to about 1%. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR010]
- Smaller differences: A06 appeared in 24 of 200 after-traces versus 6 of 200 before-traces (about 12% versus 3%, based on small counts), and A19 now precedes A27 by two positions in about 108 of 200 after-traces, a relation seen in only 1 of 200 before-traces. [OCC002, LAG005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a reordering hypothesis: in the later window, the segment formed by A35, A36, A41, A42 and A43 is executed after A27 and A26, whereas in the before window it was executed before them, with entry and exit points rewired accordingly — A25 now leads to A27, A26 now leads into the group, and the group flows into A30, which previously followed A26 directly. This is shown directly by the order flip between the two segments at full co-occurrence in both windows, and it is consistently echoed by the successor changes at A25, A26 and the group members and by the opposite position shifts of the two segments; with about 65 qualifying control-flow items against roughly one expected for an unchanged process, the ensemble is not what a stable process typically produces. This remains a possibility supported by the evidence, not a confirmed modification. [REL011, REL016, REL018, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, POS002, POS003, POS004]

Limitations: each window shows essentially a single ordering, so a changed mix of two pre-existing orderings cannot be ruled out; the item count overstates independence because the relational, directional and positional items describe the same underlying behaviour from different angles; and the lag-based corroboration rests on only 1–3 after-observations per pair. [REL011, REL012, REL013, LAG010, LAG011, LAG012, LAG013, LAG014]

Other differences: A02's participation dropped from about 32% to about 10% of traces, it now appears later in the trace when present, and its surroundings were rewired, including the near-disappearance of A46's transitions into A02 — a participation and routing change distinct from the reordering hypothesis. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR010] A06 appeared in 24 of 200 after-traces versus 6 of 200 before-traces, though both counts are small. [OCC002] A19 now typically precedes A27 by two positions in about 108 of 200 after-traces, a relation almost absent before. [LAG005]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Screening: 193 units tested, 65 items qualified, expected without change: 0.96. That's a count many times larger than expected by chance (65 vs ~1). So the screening comparison says the number of items cannot be explained by chance as a whole. So we move past "insufficient evidence" at the screening level.

Now, all items are control-flow family (OCC, DIR, POS, REL, LAG). No time (TWAIT) or resource (ASSIGN, CONC, HAND) items. So I must not discuss time or resources.

Let me understand the behavioural story.

OCC001: A02 participation dropped from ~0.315 (about 63 in 200 traces) to 0.10 (about 20 in 200 traces). Mean occurrences per trace 0.325 → 0.11. So A02 became much rarer.

OCC002: A06 participation increased from 0.03 (6 traces) to 0.12 (24 traces). Small numbers though.

DIR001: outgoing transitions of A02 redistributed. Before: mostly A20 (0.46) and A19 (0.38), plus small others. After: A02's outgoing transitions now spread across many activities: A52 (0.23), A38 (0.14), A19 (0.09), A50 (0.09), and many small ones. A20 and A19 no longer dominant. Support before 65, after 22 — few observations after, so weak.

DIR002: A15's outgoing transitions: before ~0.99 to A16; after ~0.95 to A16. Tiny change (observed_change 0.000286 cosine dissimilarity — actually very small). The characterization says redistributed but the change is tiny; A16 remains dominant in both. This is essentially stable. Note empirical_strength is 0.995 for everything — that seems to be a quirk (all items have same strength). Hmm, all items have empirical_strength 0.9950248756218906. That's suspicious — it's the same for every item, which suggests the empirical strength is not very discriminative here. I should rely on observed changes and support.

DIR003: A25's outgoing transitions: before spread across A41 (0.22), A43 (0.20), A35 (0.19), A36 (0.19), A42 (0.18); after: 0.99 to A27. Massive change. Support 201 before, 200 after — substantial.

DIR004: A26's outgoing: before ~0.98 to A30; after spread across A42 (0.21), A41 (0.21), A35 (0.19), A36 (0.18), A43 (0.16), A30 (0.005). Massive change. Support 201/201.

DIR005: A35's outgoing: before A43 (0.23), A42 (0.19), A27 (0.17), A36 (0.20), A41 (0.19); after A42 (0.23), A30 (0.19), A41 (0.20), A43 (0.19), A36 (0.17). So A27 replaced by A30. Moderate change 0.178.

DIR006: A36's outgoing: before A27 (0.21), A42 (0.24), A41 (0.18), A35 (0.15), A43 (0.19); after A41 (0.20), A35 (0.20), A43 (0.20), A42 (0.19), A30 (0.18). Again A27 → A30 swap.

DIR007: A41's outgoing: before A35 (0.225), A43 (0.23), A27 (0.175), A42 (0.17), A36 (0.18); after A43 (0.185), A36 (0.23), A42 (0.17), A30 (0.195), A35 (0.21). A27 → A30 again.

DIR008: A42's outgoing: before A36 (0.205), A41 (0.195), A35 (0.25), A27 (0.21), A43 (0.13); after A36 (0.154), A43 (0.244), A41 (0.144), A35 (0.214), A30 (0.214). A27 → A30.

DIR009: A43's outgoing: before A42 (0.2), A36 (0.215), A27 (0.22), A41 (0.195), A35 (0.16); after A30 (0.20), A41 (0.23), A35 (0.15), A42 (0.16), A36 (0.24). A27 → A30.

So consistent pattern: in the before window, A25, A26, A35, A36, A41, A42, A43 all had outgoing transitions to A27 (and A26 went to A30). In the after window, A27 disappeared as a successor and A30 appeared instead. So A27 was replaced by A30 as the successor of this whole group of activities.

POS003: A27's position moved earlier: mean position 0.52 → 0.39, median 0.525 → 0.38. Support 1.0 in both (A27 in all traces). So A27 still occurs in all traces but earlier.

POS002: A26's position moved earlier: mean 0.654 → 0.517. Support 1.0 both.

POS004-POS008: A35, A36, A41, A42, A43 positions moved later: mean ~0.44 → ~0.60. Support 1.0 both.

So the group A35, A36, A41, A42, A43 moved later in the trace, while A26 and A27 moved earlier.

REL011–REL020: pairs (A26,A35), (A26,A36), (A26,A41), (A26,A42), (A26,A43), (A27,A35), (A27,A36), (A27,A41), (A27,A42), (A27,A43): before, B_before_A ~0.99 (i.e., A35/A36/A41/A42/A43 came before A26/A27); after, A_before_B ~0.98 (A26/A27 come before A35..A43). So the order between {A26, A27} and {A35, A36, A41, A42, A43} flipped: previously the A35–A43 group ran before A26/A27; now A26/A27 run before the A35–A43 group. Co-occurrence stays 1.0 — both always in same trace.

LAG items: many show changes but with tiny after-support (1–3 observations). E.g., LAG005: (A19,A27) before support 1, after 108 — before it was lag 1 in 1 observation, after lag 2 in 108. Hmm, that's interesting: A19→A27 with lag 2 in 108 after-traces. But before support only 1. LAG020/021: (A46,A19), (A46,A20) with decent support both windows: lag mostly 1, slightly more concentrated at 1 after. LAG022: (A46,A25): lag 2 in 0.705 before, 0.93 after; support 200/200.

That's consistent with the ordering flip: A25 now goes to A27 (DIR003), and A35–A43 come after A26/A27... wait, actually let me think about the structure.

- A27 at position ~0.52.

- A35–A43 each have outgoing to A27 (~0.17–0.22 each) plus to each other (A35→A43, A42, A36, A41; etc.). So the group {A35, A36, A41, A42, A43} is a mutually connected block, and each also connects to A27.

Hmm wait, but A35–A43 go to A30 in the after window, and A26 goes into the block. And A27 at position 0.39 comes before A26 at 0.52? REL pairs between A27 and block: after, A27 before block. And A25 → A27.

So after: A25 → A27 → A26 → block {A35..A43} → A30. Before: A25 → block → A27 → A26 → A30.

Hmm, interesting: A26 → A30 before; after, block → A30. And A26 now feeds the block.

So essentially the block {A35, A36, A41, A42, A43} moved from before A27/A26 to after A27/A26. A27 and A26 moved earlier (positions 0.52→0.39, 0.65→0.52), block moved later (0.44→0.60). The successor of the block changed from A27 to A30; the successor of A26 changed from A30 to the block; A25's successor changed from the block to A27.

This is a reordering/swap of segments: the segment {A35–A43} and the segment {A27, A26} swapped their relative order. REL011–REL020 directly show the order flip between {A26,A27} and the block, with co-occurrence 1.0 in both windows (both always present). This is direct relational evidence of an ordering change — a swap of positions of two groups.

Also A02: participation dropped from ~32% to ~10% of traces, and its outgoing transitions changed completely (before mostly A19/A20; after spread across many including A52, A38). POS001 shows A02's position moved later (median 0.32 → 0.75) among the traces where it occurs. LAG001–LAG004 show A02's lag to A19/A36/A41/A43 changed, but after-support is tiny (1–3). REL001–REL010 show A02 co-occurrence with many activities dropped from 0.315 to 0.10 — that's just the A02 participation drop reflected in pairs (same trace behaviour, not independent confirmation).

OCC002: A06 participation rose 0.03 → 0.12 (6 → 24 traces). Small numbers; weak.

Now the hypothesis: The main hypothesis is a structural/ordering change: the block of activities A35, A36, A41, A42, A43, which previously executed before A27 and A26 (and were entered from A25), now execute after A27 and A26 (entered from A26, followed by A30). I.e., the two segments swapped order. This is supported directly by REL011–REL020 (order flip with full co-occurrence), DIR003–DIR009 (successor changes: A25 now → A27; A26 now → block; block now → A30 instead of A27), and POS002/POS003/POS004–POS008 (position shifts consistent with the swap: A26, A27 earlier; block later).

Is this "a change between a fixed order and mixed order" or "exchange of positions"? It's an exchange of positions / reordering of two groups — a hypothesis about order/placement, which needs relational or positional evidence. We have REL and POS and DIR successor changes. Good.

The "shift in path frequencies" caveat: this is not a shift in path frequencies; it's a reordering (positions swapped, successors changed). The condition about "every activity observed in substantial share in both windows" applies to path-frequency hypotheses; here activities are all in 100% of traces in both windows (support 1.0 for POS002–POS008; REL co-occurrence 1.0). So it's not a participation change for these; it's a reordering.

Now the A02 change is a separate difference: A02 participation dropped from ~32% to ~10% of traces, and its outgoing transitions changed completely (before mostly A19/A20; after spread across many including A52, A38). POS001 shows A02's position moved later (median 0.32 → 0.75) among the traces where it occurs. LAG001–LAG004 show A02's lag to A19/A36/A41/A43 changed, but after-support is tiny (1–3). These suggest A46's transitions to A19/A20 became more immediately adjacent. Modest changes. Could be reported as other differences, though they're small. After the swap, A25 → A27 directly (lag 1), and the block is after A26, so A25 to A35 distance is now larger than 5. I shouldn't over-speculate. The main, well-supported story is the swap of the two segments. The A02 decline is a second, also well-supported difference (OCC001 with support 63/20, DIR001 though after-support only 22, POS001, REL001–010 co-occurrence drop). A02's participation drop is a participation change: activity executed in fewer traces. That's a hypothesis in its own right (part of the process executed less often / became rarer). But is it part of the main hypothesis or "other differences"? It involves A02, A19, A20 and many others; it's separate from the block swap. I'd report it under "Other differences".

Actually wait — could the A02 drop be connected? A02 before went to A19/A20; A19/A20 relate to A46 (LAG020/021: A46→A19, A46→A20). So A02's decline is corroborated by DIR010 (A46's transitions to A02 nearly disappeared). But note DIR shares are over outgoing transitions, not cases.

So the main hypothesis: reordering — the group A35, A36, A41, A42, A43 and the pair A27/A26 swapped their order in the process. Before: after A25, the block ran first, then A27, then A26, which led to A30. After: A25 leads to A27, A27/A26 run earlier, A26 feeds the block, and the block now leads to A30.
